\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Applications}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Products.Applications
\section{Overview}
Finite-product hypercontractivity bounds the stability of small events and the stable influences of Boolean functions. Quantitative KKL inequalities and Friedgut junta approximation follow with explicit dependence on the minimum atom mass.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Stability as a noisy squared norm]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_stability_sq_eq_norm_noise_sq}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.condExp_selfAdjoint, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_const_mul, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_sum, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.stability, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationAux.component_noise}
\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $c\in\mathbb R$, and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Then $\operatorname{Stab}_{c^2}(f)=\|T_cf\|_{2,P}^2$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $T_a h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a^{|S|}h_S$ for every real rate $a$; $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$; $\operatorname{Stab}_a(h)=\mathbb E_P[hT_a h]$. The powers indexed by subset cardinalities are natural powers, including $0^0=1$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_indicator_norm_sq}
\leanok

\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, an event $A\subseteq\Omega$, and $p>0$. Then $\|\mathbf1_A\|_{p,P}^2=\Pr_P(A)^{2/p}$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$; $\Pr_P(A)=\mathbb E_P\mathbf1_A$, where $\mathbf1_A$ is $1$ on $A$ and $0$ elsewhere.
\end{theorem}

The powers indexed by subset cardinalities are natural powers, including $0^0=1$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_stableInfluence_eq_sq_norm_noise_laplacian}

\difficulty{5}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $\rho\ge0$, a coordinate $i$, and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Then $\rho I_i^{(\rho)}(f)=\|T_{\sqrt\rho}L_if\|_{2,P}^2$, where $I_i^{(\rho)}$ is stable influence and $L_i$ is the coordinate Laplacian. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $T_a h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a^{|S|}h_S$ for every real rate $a$; $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$; $L_i h=h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h$; $I_i^{(a)}(h)=\sum_{S\ni i}a^{|S|-1}\mathbb E_Ph_S^2$ for $a\in\mathbb R$. The powers indexed by subset cardinalities are natural powers, including $0^0=1$.
\end{theorem}

Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ with every coordinate atom at least $0<\lambda\le1/2$. If $f:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$ has positive variance and $a=I(f)/\operatorname{Var}_P(f)$, there is a coordinate $i$ such that $(a^{-1})^2(9/\lambda)^{-a}\le I_i(f)$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $I_i(h)=\mathbb E_P(h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h)^2$; $I(h)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}I_i(h)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}|S|\mathbb E_Ph_S^2$; $\operatorname{Var}_P(h)=\mathbb E_P(h-\mathbb E_Ph)^2$.
\end{theorem}
